Messages.Author: Jeff Grubb
Messages.Body:
Has anyone else noticed this one?

Ambrosius, the Ferryman (AH) Ally - Giovanni (Very faint on my copy) -
cost 3 blood - Unique Ally, with 2 life, 1 hand damage, 0 bleed. Ambrosius
is immune to damage that is not aggravated. He can take an action to allow
you to move a retainer from your ash heap to a ready vampire you control.
Put 3 Pathos counters on the retainer. Remove a Pathos counter from the
retainer at the beginning of each of your minion phases. When there are no
Pathos counters remaining, remove the retainer from the game.

PLUS

Zombie (DS) Retainer - Giovanni - Cost 1 blood - Retainer with 2 life,
whish says several things about combat, then ends with "As a +1 Stealth
aciton, the controlling vampire may burn the Zombie to gain 2 blood.

EQUALS

Put Ambrosius into play. Discard a Zombie to the Ash Heap. Use Ambrosious'
ability to put the Zombie on a vampire low on blood. Then burn the Zombie
(before placing any Pathos counters) for two blood, returning it to the
Ash Heap. Repeat every turn to keep your vampires healthy.

Is this correct? Have I missed something on this combo?

Jeff G.

>Put Ambrosius into play. Discard a Zombie to the Ash Heap. Use Ambrosious'
>ability to put the Zombie on a vampire low on blood. Then burn the Zombie
>(before placing any Pathos counters) for two blood, returning it to the
>Ash Heap. Repeat every turn to keep your vampires healthy.
>
>Is this correct? Have I missed something on this combo?

No problem - you've just taken two actions (one at +1 stealth) to put
two blood onto a vampire.

Similar to having the target hunt and having Leonardo the Mortician
put a blood on him, except that both of these actions are at stealth.

Not a very awesome combo.

Peace Pat, but notice that the Zombie would be removed from the game ONLY IF
THE PATHOS COUNTERS RUN OUT, as you underlined. The intent of this combo. is
to burn the zombie before the pathos counters run out, thus keeping it in the
game. There is no reason to believe that a card in the ash heap should retain
state (i.e. the number of pathos counters previously on it).

Messages.Author: Paul Echeverri
Messages.Body:
In article <Pine.SOL.3.91.960607163801.25230C-100000@freenet>,

<mal...@macatawa.org> wrote:
>On Thu, 6 Jun 1996, The Corrupter wrote:

[ambrosius/zombie combo elided]

>I would think that you couldn't burn the Zombie before the Pathos

>counters were placed on it.. thus after three turns, this combo goes
>boom. Just my HO.

You're not burning the Zombie before the Pathos counters are placed; you're
burning it before the *last* counter is removed; thus, the remove-from-game
condition never kicks in. It's a nice, viable combo, but as (I believe)
L. Scott Johnson pointed out, not particularly devastating. It's maybe
a smidgen better than hunting.

Well, the combo does have merits over those that you mentioned:

It's not fortitude based (i.e. Giovanni can use it as a clan).
It's not equipment that Gangrels can Bum's Rush then Canine
Horde (or fast hands for any celerity deck).
It's not a location that can be stolen or burned.

It's all a matter of preference and situation, but it's nice to see
another combo that can produce the same results :)

Messages.Author: DOUGDWISE
Messages.Body:
Well, if we are looking for another combo that produces the same results:
First- Vampire hunts: gains 1 blood, uses 1 action
Next- Vampire hunts: gains 1 blood, uses 1 action
So for a cost of 2 actions your vampire gets 2 blood. OK, so it does tie
up your vampire for two turns instead of allowing him to bleed or call
votes but if he is in danger from low blood, you probably want him to lie
low anyway.
I just don't see this Ferryman combo being that useful.
Doug
